source.title: Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers
source.authors: Kristóf Váradi; Márk Marosi; Peter Antal

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; no material cut-off or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study replaces residual-stream activations with SAE reconstructions and measures the resulting cross-entropy change. This is relevant to V3, but it does not compare against random errors of the same size.
record.gate_note: Table 10 reports activation-replacement cross-entropy changes by layer and SAE expansion factor. Those outcomes do not establish whether reconstruction errors are more harmful than matched random errors. The paper also reports generation validity after replacement, but that does not measure V3's loss comparison or the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper uses ReLU SAEs as a tool to interpret a 25M-parameter SMILES transformer. Its only dark-matter-adjacent result is the splice-in ΔCE/KL quality check in Table 10 (Sec. E.1). That check has no matched random-error baseline, so it cannot show whether SAE errors are pathological (V3). There are no per-token error norms or cross-size error overlap (V2), no linear prediction of the error (V1, V4), no circuit or steering analysis with versus without the error term (V5), and no architecture or objective comparison (V6). Sec. 2.1 says only that newer SAE variants improve on the ReLU baseline. The record's 'tests/T2' should be changed to uses_without_test/T4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for Sec. E.1: fidelity generally improves with SAE size, and reconstruction is hardest in L3–L4. It should note the L0 exception. It should also say this is a side check. The paper's main conclusions are about ring and branch syntax circuits, a linear valence direction, chemically meaningful SAE features, and SAE features being useful for property prediction and steering. The authors draw no conclusion about SAE dark matter.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates decoded SAE activation replacement and output fidelity; it does not report the dark-matter error analysis. The original method is not specified in this text.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and SAE expansion factor affect the reported cross-entropy changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Splice-in ΔCE generally falls with dictionary size (e.g. L1: 0.032 to 0.016; L3: 0.103 to 0.058) but stays nonzero. It peaks in the middle layers (L3–L4, about 0.10) and is flat at L5 (about 0.03). At L0 it is non-monotonic: 4x gives 0.031 while 8x gives 0.046.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a small molecular transformer, SAE splice-in loss shrinks with dictionary size but persists, and is largest in middle layers.

record.problems: No matched random-error baseline for the SAE reconstruction loss comparison; results concern one 25M-parameter molecular transformer. Table 10 reports means without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from Table 10 for the reported cross-entropy metric. Generation-validity outcomes are not extracted because they do not measure the loss comparison in V3.

untested.parts: All: no linear regression of the SAE error on the input activation.
All: no per-token error norms, no cross-size predictability, and no analysis of whether different sizes fail on the same contexts. Only aggregate ΔCE across sizes is reported.
All: no matched-norm random-error baseline for the splice-in loss.
All: no decomposition of the error into linear and nonlinear parts.
All: the circuit analyses (head ablations) do not use SAEs. SAE steering is run without any comparison that keeps versus drops the error term.
All: only ReLU SAEs are trained, with no architecture, objective or end-to-end comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Single 25M-parameter SMILES model with ReLU SAEs and ghost grads, trained to L0 of 10–50. Table 10 values are means with no uncertainty. The paper reports ΔCE and KL but not the clean or ablation loss, so the fraction of loss recovered cannot be computed. The rows are better treated as context than as a test of V3.

versions.untested_parts: No test of linear predictability of the SAE error from input activations.

Although reconstruction fidelity is reported across SAE sizes, the study does not measure per-token error norms, their predictability across sizes, overlap in contexts where different sizes fail, or whether the error itself vanishes with scale.
The study reports loss after SAE reconstruction but does not compare it with random errors of the same size.
No decomposition of error into linear and nonlinear parts, or test of whether these correspond to unlearned versus resistant features.
No comparison of circuit or steering analyses with and without the SAE error term.
No comparison of SAE training artifacts, alternative architectures, or end-to-end training as explanations for dark matter.
